schema: narrative analysis, regenerated whenever new data lands. the deterministic engine finds the facts; this reads them.
headline: The project has its first warm owner-side lead and its first real outreach data on the same day. The lead is a full 640-acre section whose owners have previously been willing to sell — and the FEMA panel puts much of it in Zone A.
state_of_play: Five brokerage contacts made in one day. One produced a lead, one had nothing at scale, two are open threads awaiting callback. That is a normal and healthy first-day hit rate.

Section 16, T92N R36W in Lincoln Township, Buena Vista County is now the most interesting record in the project: one full PLSS section, 640 acres exactly, off-market, at $12,000-12,500 an acre — roughly $7.7 to $8.0 million.
It is also the most compromised. The FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer shows Zone A across much of the section, sourced from the North Raccoon River, with no Base Flood Elevation determined.
Buena Vista County now holds two of the eighteen sites on record. It scores 78 on the screen with 3.4 owners per section — comfortably in the workable tier, though not the top of it.
Ten of the top twelve counties still hold no position, and none of the six tier-one contacts have been approached. The outreach so far has all been to land brokerages.

what_the_data_says.point: Zone A without a Base Flood Elevation is a harder problem than ordinary floodplain
what_the_data_says.detail: Zone A means FEMA mapped the 1% annual chance floodplain but never ran the hydraulic analysis to establish how deep the water gets. There is no number to design against. Elevating or filling a campus requires commissioning that study first, which is time and money spent before you know whether the site is viable. The 416-acre net figure on record applies the standard floodplain haircut and should be treated as an upper bound — a visual read of the panel suggests the true buildable share is lower.

what_the_data_says.point: The section geometry is exactly the thesis, which makes the flood finding more frustrating
what_the_data_says.detail: This is a single PLSS section — 640 acres under what appears to be unified ownership, on the Des Moines Lobe, with section-line road access on all four sides. Structurally it is the ideal unit. The constraint is water, not assemblage.

what_the_data_says.point: A willing owner is the scarcest thing in the dataset
what_the_data_says.detail: Seventeen of the eighteen sites are public listings or unapproached strangers. This one has owners who have previously entertained a sale. That is worth preserving as a relationship even if this particular section does not survive diligence — the same owners may hold or know of other ground.

what_the_data_says.point: The brokerage channel is working, but it is the shallow end
what_the_data_says.detail: Five calls produced one lead. High Point's best was 107 acres near Davenport, which is an order of magnitude too small and tells you what general land brokerages carry. The channels that reach large contiguous ground — utility development groups, regional partnerships, the state certified-site register — remain untouched.

what_the_data_says.point: One number in the log is unqualified and larger than everything else
what_the_data_says.detail: A 2,700+ acre figure sits against Iowa Farmland with no location, parcel count or owner attached, and the contact was made through a website form rather than a conversation. It is either the largest opportunity in the project or a portfolio total across scattered listings. A phone call settles which.

watchlist: Section 16 needs a delineated buildable acreage before any offer. Ask the broker whether a survey or elevation certificate exists, and whether the non-flood ground is contiguous or fragmented.
Zone A boundaries are drawn approximately. A Letter of Map Amendment could move them, but that is a study, not a phone call.
Trevor Glomski at High Point asked to be called back with changes — that thread only stays warm if it is worked.
The 2,700+ acre Iowa Farmland figure has been sitting unqualified since first contact.
Still no owner names anywhere in the dataset except this one, and even here the owners are known only through the broker.
if_nothing_else: Two calls. Back to Matt Skinner to ask what share of Section 16 sits outside Zone A and whether the non-flood ground is contiguous — that single answer decides whether this is an $8M site or a dead one. Then Iowa Farmland by phone, to find out whether 2,700 acres means one block or a portfolio.
